qAndA.answer: The yellow lines, marked by yellow cones and disks, represent a trigger for the defenders to press. When the attacking team's ball crosses this line, the defenders move forward to try and win the ball back.
qAndA.question: What are the 'yellow lines' in the drill, and what purpose do they serve?

qAndA.answer: The Coach stresses the importance of pace in attacking. If the attackers move quickly enough, they can create an advantageous 3v2 situation after breaking the yellow line.
qAndA.question: What does the Coach emphasize as a critical aspect of the drill?

qAndA.answer: The Coach advises Rudy to make more clever diagonal runs instead of running in straight lines, making it harder for the defenders to mark him.
qAndA.question: What specific advice does the Coach give to the attacker named Rudy?

youtube_description:
To view this video and to have access to the printable session plan, visit:
https://thecoachingmanual.com/drill/5697070107197440

This attacking overloads session develops an understanding of when to pass and when to dribble and teaches players the principles of fast-break counter-attacks.

This challenging opposed practice encourages players to play with a quick tempo, to make clever movements and to break lines i.e. try to get beyond the defender. It also tests players' decision-making as they are challenged to make the most of an overload situation.
